text: I think the strongest argument for protecting study time on campus is very simple, it is about how the brain actually works when we try to learn something hard. When I am reading for my chemistry class and somebody talks to me or my phone buzz, I lose my place and I must start the paragraph again, so the real time I waste is more than the interruption itself. If the university wants students to do good work, then giving us quiet hours and quiet spaces is not just a comfort thing, it is a basic condition for learning to even happen. Some people will say students can just find their own focus and stop blaming the environment, but this is not fair to everyone equally. Many of us live with roommates or work part time jobs, so the library or a protected study room is the only place where we have a chance to concentrate fully. For these reasons I believe protecting uninterrupted study time is the most defensible argument, because it helps the students who need it the most and it costs the campus almost nothing to do.
